newsitem.title: USA: U.S. sees no cause for concern in Syrian maneuvers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. sees no cause for concern in Syrian maneuvers.

text.p: The United States said on Tuesday it saw no cause for concern over recent Syrian troop movements which have caused anxiety in Israel.
"I know of nothing in our own eyes, here ... that would lead us to any kind of cause of undue concern," State Department Nicholas Burns told a questioner at a routine news briefing.

"A lot of people in this government do watch that question closely. And we would obviously be taking certain steps if we thought there was some kind of possibility of imminent conflict here," Burns said.
"We don't believe that's the case. And we believe that both the governments of Syria and Israel understand the catastrophic consequences of any kind of conflict along the border."
A series of Syrian army exercises and troop movements close to the Israeli border have given Israelis war jitters.
Syrian Foreign Minister Farouq al-Shara on Tuesday said Syria was not preparing for an attack on Israel and accused Israeli leaders of making the accusation to avoid making peace.

Israel's ambassador to Washington, Eliahu Ben Elissar, said on Monday that Israeli concerns had partly although not entirely abated following Syrian assurances through the United States that these were routine autumn manoeuvres.
Israel itself ended a huge military exercise in the Golan Heights on Tuesday involving war planes, tanks and artillery units. An Israeli army spokesman described these manoeuvres too as routine.
